sports.name: Gym & Hypertrophy
sports.summary: Optimized for progressive overload, myofibrillar muscle protein synthesis, and nervous system recovery.
sports.preWorkout: 30-45g complex carbs + 20g protein 90 min before training. Adequate sodium for cellular pump.
sports.duringWorkout: 500-750ml water with electrolytes if workout exceeds 60 min. Intra-workout EAAs optional.
sports.postWorkout: 30-40g rapid-digesting whey or plant protein with 40-60g carbs within 90 minutes.

sports.name: Running & Marathon
sports.summary: Focuses on sustained glycogen availability, gastric comfort, and electrolyte loss mitigation.
sports.preWorkout: Easily digestible low-fiber carbs (banana, toast, white rice) 1-2 hours prior. Minimal fat.
sports.duringWorkout: 30-60g carbohydrate gels or drink mix per hour on runs over 70 minutes.
sports.postWorkout: 4:1 Carb-to-protein ratio immediately post-run to accelerate glycogen resynthesis.

sports.name: Cycling & Peloton
sports.summary: High hourly caloric expenditure requiring steady intra-ride carbohydrate and fluid replacement.
sports.preWorkout: Oatmeal with berries and a light protein source 2-3 hours before wheels up.
sports.duringWorkout: 60-90g dual-source (glucose/fructose) carbs/hour for high-intensity or long climbs.
sports.postWorkout: Electrolyte rehydration drink followed by a nutrient-dense whole food meal within 2 hours.

sports.name: Football & Soccer
sports.summary: Demands both aerobic stamina and explosive phosphagen sprint intervals across 90+ minutes.
sports.preWorkout: Balanced moderate-glycemic meal 3 hours prior; light fruit or bar 45 mins before kickoff.
sports.duringWorkout: Isotonic electrolyte beverage at halftime with 20-30g fast-acting carbohydrates.
sports.postWorkout: High-antioxidant recovery meal with tart cherry juice, lean poultry or paneer, and quinoa.

sports.name: Cricket
sports.summary: Prolonged heat exposure and intermittent explosive bursts requiring temperature regulation and mental clarity.
sports.preWorkout: Hydrating, electrolyte-balanced meal with slow-digesting grains (millets, oats) and curd.
sports.duringWorkout: Electrolyte rehydration solution every 30 minutes in humid or hot pitch conditions.
sports.postWorkout: Rehydration at 150% of weight lost, coupled with anti-inflammatory recovery foods.

sports.name: Swimming & Aquatic
sports.summary: Submerged activity with high caloric burn and hidden sweat rates that often deceive sensation.
sports.preWorkout: Light, non-greasy carbs 60-90 mins prior to prevent esophageal reflux during horizontal swimming.
sports.duringWorkout: Sip electrolyte water poolside every 20-30 laps.
sports.postWorkout: Warm recovery shake or broth with complete proteins and warm complex carbohydrates.

sports.name: Yoga & Pilates
sports.summary: Focuses on myofascial flexibility, joint lubrication, and cellular anti-inflammatory nutrition.
sports.preWorkout: Light hydration with lemon water or coconut water 45 mins before practice. Empty stomach preferred.
sports.duringWorkout: Room temperature water as needed between flows.
sports.postWorkout: Clean protein bowl with leafy greens, healthy fats (avocado, nuts), and anti-inflammatory spices (turmeric).

sports.name: General Active Lifestyle
sports.summary: Foundational clinical nutrition designed for sustainable daily energy, fat management, and vitality.
sports.preWorkout: Whole food balance: whole fruit, handful of almonds, or a cup of green tea.
sports.duringWorkout: Plain water throughout moderate 45-60 minute sessions.
sports.postWorkout: Balanced Mediterranean or clinical plate: 1/2 vegetables, 1/4 clean protein, 1/4 complex carb.

recipes.title: Clinical Green Power Smoothie
ingredients: 1 cup Unsweetened Almond Milk or Coconut Water
recipes.instructions: Blend all ingredients on high until silky smooth. Top with pumpkin seeds and fresh blueberries for an antioxidant boost.

recipes.title: High-Protein Quinoa & Spiced Paneer
ingredients: 150g Low-fat Paneer (or firm Tofu) cut into cubes
recipes.instructions: Lightly sear the spiced paneer in olive oil for 4 minutes. Plate over warm fluffy quinoa and steamed greens. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over top.

recipes.title: Glycogen Replenish Overnight Oats
ingredients: 1 scoop Vanilla Whey or Pea Protein
recipes.instructions: Mix oats, protein, flaxseed, and milk in a mason jar. Chill overnight. Top with fresh berries and raw honey before morning training.

recipes.title: Omega-3 Rich Salmon & Sweet Potato
ingredients: 1 medium Roasted Sweet Potato with skin
Sea Salt, Cracked Black Pepper, Dill
recipes.instructions: Season salmon with dill and sea salt. Pan-sear for 4 mins each side until crispy yet tender. Serve alongside baked sweet potato and garlic asparagus.

goals.title: Muscle Gain & Hypertrophy
goals.desc: Hypercaloric protocols and precise protein timing for maximal tissue synthesis and strength gains.
goals.carbTarget: 4.0 - 7.0 g per kg to sustain intense lifting
goals.clinicalFocus: Optimize leucine threshold (3g per feeding) every 3-4 hours to trigger mTOR signaling.

goals.title: Fat Loss & Preservation
goals.desc: Hypocaloric strategies focusing on satiety, micronutrient density, and lean mass preservation.
goals.proteinTarget: 2.0 - 2.4 g per kg to prevent catabolic breakdown
goals.carbTarget: 2.0 - 3.5 g per kg timed around workouts
goals.clinicalFocus: High thermic effect of food (TEF), 30g+ daily dietary fiber, and high hydration to regulate ghrelin.

goals.title: Aerobic & Endurance Peak
goals.desc: Maximizing glycogen resynthesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, and optimal power-to-weight ratio.
goals.caloricRule: Isocaloric to slight surplus on high-mileage blocks
goals.proteinTarget: 1.4 - 1.7 g per kg for muscle repair
goals.carbTarget: 6.0 - 10.0 g per kg depending on training duration
goals.clinicalFocus: Gut carbohydrate absorption capacity (glucose:fructose 2:1) and electrolyte replenishment.

goals.title: Cellular Recovery & Longevity
goals.desc: Systemic reduction of oxidative stress, joint cartilage support, and endocrine hormonal balance.
goals.caloricRule: Maintenance with nutrient-dense bioavailable whole foods
goals.proteinTarget: 1.4 - 1.8 g per kg with high collagen/glycine content
goals.carbTarget: 3.0 - 4.5 g per kg low-glycemic antioxidant-rich sources
goals.clinicalFocus: Polyphenols, Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA), Magnesium glycinate, and sleep hygiene.

prescription.goalStrategy: +400 kcal lean surplus to optimize myofibrillar protein synthesis
